topics.overview: Aiden Agent is an AI workspace application for desktop and a headless server (`aiden serve`), with paired native iOS and Android companions. It supports conversations, configured local or hosted models, workspace tools, optional memory, skills, Web Search, scheduled tasks and supported device tools. Availability depends on platform, setup, permissions and the current chat. Ask for a feature's controls to view its real settings in chat. Experimental or developer-plan features are not promises of installed capabilities.
topics.how-agents-work: Your selected model produces responses and requests tools. Aiden executes admitted tools on the serving host and returns results to the model. Workspace access, app policy and domain permissions determine which effects are allowed. Local models may keep inference on your machine; hosted providers receive the request context. Compaction summarizes older context when needed. Aiden uses Pi as its agent engine. It does not gain access to other chats or devices merely because they appear in the app.
topics.memory: Memory can retain useful facts for future conversations. Global Memory and the selected workspace's Memory gate are separate. Turning Memory off stops future admitted use; it does not delete saved facts or remove context already sent to a model. View Memory controls to see the current gates. To see or delete what Aiden remembers in a workspace, open Settings → Memory → What Aiden remembers; deleting a fact there removes it for good. Bots keep their own memory on each Bot's page.
topics.web-search: Web Search uses the host's configured provider route and credentials. Enabling its switch does not run a search or fetch a model catalog. Setup and actual tool readiness are distinct from the saved enabled preference. Search results are external information, not permission to change app settings.
topics.skills: Skills are instructions that guide the agent for particular tasks. They do not grant permissions or execute app administration by themselves. Aiden includes an immutable aiden-app skill for product questions and controls. The global Skills switch disables skill discovery and use, including the built-in skill. Separately owned product-help functions remain available so you can learn how to restore Skills.
topics.appearance: Appearance changes presentation. On the desktop, Aiden can change the color mode (System, Light or Dark), the color theme, chat width and Reduce Motion from chat. Custom theme colors are edited in Settings → Appearance, and View → Zoom In or Zoom Out makes everything bigger or smaller. A paired phone has its own native appearance preferences; a control labeled Paired host changes that host, not the phone. The headless server has no appearance settings of its own.
topics.privacy: Product help is bundled and read offline. A chat-control click calls Aiden's settings service directly without another inference request. Controls never expose provider keys. Remote controls require a current pairing and applicable grants; a phone is a client of the serving host. Turning features off cannot undo information previously sent to a model. Model catalog and benchmark refreshes remain explicit foreground actions.
topics.setup: Configure providers, authentication, Computer Use and other sensitive capabilities through Aiden's existing trusted Settings and permission flows. Opening setup does not authenticate, fetch catalogs or grant execution automatically. Product controls expose supported preferences only; they do not provide arbitrary shell commands or UI automation. Check the current capability projection before assuming a feature is available.
topics.changing-settings: From chat, Aiden can change only the supported app controls that aiden_get_state lists: color mode, color theme, chat width, Reduce Motion and the model for new chats on the desktop, and the Memory, Workspace memory, Web Search and Skills switches. Settings → Appearance → Controls in chat decides whether Aiden may change them (Disabled, Ask every time or Safe controls); turning a feature back on needs your click on the control. Everything else stays in Settings: custom theme colors, providers, API keys, connectors, tool approvals, Computer Use, Bots, voice, notifications and keyboard shortcuts. When Aiden cannot make a change it should say so and point to the right Settings page. In a chat from a paired phone, Aiden can only show the controls; you change them yourself, and only when Paired-device chat controls is on.
topics.models: Pick a model for a chat from the model menu in the composer. A chat that already has messages keeps its own model; picking one in an empty chat sets the default for new chats, and on the desktop Aiden can change the model for new chats from chat. Add providers, sign in or enter API keys in Settings → Providers, and compare models in Settings → Model Pad. Aiden cannot add providers or keys from chat.
topics.voice: Dictate into the composer with voice input where your device supports it. Set up dictation in Settings → Voice and spoken replies in Settings → Text to Speech. Aiden Live, the real-time voice and screen companion, is set up in Settings → Aiden Live. These settings are not changed from chat.
topics.bots: Bots are separate agents you create from the sidebar. Each Bot has its own chats, memory, files, routines and access rules. You change a Bot's access and settings in that Bot's own settings, not from a normal chat. A Bot asks before risky steps and hands sign-ins and payments back to you.

skill.name: aiden-app
skill.description: Explain Aiden's shipped abilities, agent behavior and privacy, and show or change its supported app controls.
skill.instructions: Use aiden_help for installed product facts and aiden_get_state for current values. For exploratory settings questions, use aiden_show_controls with the relevant topic. For an explicit permitted request, use aiden_set_preference and report only its verified result. Never invent current values, model inventories, permissions or shipped features. Distinguish session, workspace, host and device scope; clarify ambiguity before widening scope. Security setup and required confirmation stay in the host's trusted flows. A skill does not grant authority.
